title: Spaghetti Bolognese
subtitle: The British home version with mince and tomato
excerpt: The weeknight bolognese that became a British institution: beef mince, tinned tomatoes, and herbs simmered until sweet and thick, served over spaghetti with grated parmesan. Not the Bolognese original, but satisfying on its own terms.

recipe.sourceNotes: The British spaghetti bolognese evolved from the Italian ragù alla bolognese into a distinct dish: quicker, with tinned tomatoes and herbs, lighter on dairy, and made with beef mince rather than a mix of meats. It became a household staple across the UK from the 1960s onward and is now one of the most cooked dishes in British homes.

recipeTools.notes: Wide enough to brown the mince without steaming.

content.text: British spaghetti bolognese is not the slow-cooked Italian ragù alla bolognese. It is its own thing: a quick, savoury mince sauce with tinned tomatoes that comes together in under an hour. The key step is browning the mince properly in a hot, wide pan so it colours rather than steams. That caramelisation gives the sauce a depth that a grey, steamed mince cannot match.
Heat the oil in a large, wide pan over medium-high heat. Add the onion, carrot, and celery and cook for 8 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook for 1 more minute.

Increase the heat to high. Add the mince and spread it across the pan. Leave it without stirring for 2 minutes to brown on the bottom, then break it up and stir. Cook for 5 minutes until the mince is browned all over and any liquid has evaporated.
Add the tomato puree and stir into the meat. Cook for 2 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes, stock, oregano, and bay leaves. Season with salt and pepper.
Bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat and cook uncovered for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce has thickened. Remove the bay leaves. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

Cook the spaghetti in a large pot of well-salted boiling water according to the packet. Drain, reserving a cup of the pasta water. Add a splash of pasta water to the sauce to loosen if needed. Toss the spaghetti with the sauce and serve with grated parmesan.
